_doc: Log-specific disruption scenarios for loan_model/disruptions.py (Phase 5), BPI Challenge 2019 (purchase-to-pay, main item category, 10% scale). The same three shock types as BPIC 2017 / BPI 2012 (D1 dispatch/system outage, D2 contact outage, D3 missing-documents surge), mapped onto this process; same lengths (72-120 h, never seen by the agent), same levels, same action set and costs.

episode._doc: cycle times are months: open items need ~150 d to settle; the horizon is set from the harm curves (Phase 5)

observation._doc: divisor of the open-cases feature (~5,000 open items at the 10% scale; the loan logs use 4,000)

recovery._doc: Same actions, costs and generic parameters as the loan logs; the meaning of each action per failure type is in its _doc. Times in working hours for handling/retry, wall-clock hours for vendor-side delays.

allowed._sla_risk: an SLA-risk alert allows the actions of the failure that blocked the case
allowed._retry: as in the loan logs: not offered in an outage (a waiting case resumes when the service is back); offered for the mismatch surge (automatic re-match)

retry._doc: invoice mismatch: an automatic re-match after delay_working_h finds the corrected document with documents_success_p, so the item skips the payment block. At most max_per_case retries per item.

payment_run_outage._doc: manual (urgent) payment outside the run: the item is paid at once, without waiting for the next run

vendor_channel_outage._doc: the vendor sends the invoice another way (e-mail / paper) and it is recorded by hand: the step is done, but the invoice arrives later

escalate._doc: a backup worker does the blocked step by hand: payment run -- an accounts-payable worker pays the item manually; vendor channel -- an accounts-payable worker records the invoice from another channel; mismatch -- a payment-block handler resolves the mismatch directly. Backup workers are real workers of the log outside the top-3 pool (the next ranks for that work item); handling time and success are assumed, as in the loan logs.

reassign._doc: invoice mismatch: the item's payment-block work goes to the front of the queue (fastest free qualified worker) and the vendor's correction is chased directly (no extra delay)

D1_payment_run_outage._doc: D1 (dispatch/system outage): the payment system is down, so a payment run in the outage pays nothing; due items fail and wait for a decision. Left alone they are paid by the first run after the restore.

D2_vendor_channel_outage._doc: D2 (contact outage): the vendor channel (EDI / portal) is down, so incoming invoices cannot be received and recorded.

D3_mismatch_surge._doc: D3 (missing-documents surge): a fault in goods-receipt / invoice data makes more invoices fail the 3-way match and get a payment block (the D3 loop, 19% of invoices normally); the vendor's correction is held up (upload_delay_h, wall-clock, added to the payment-block visit). Each item routed to the block during the surge is a decision.

training_cycle._doc: One cell per scenario, length drawn per episode (72-120 h), as for the loan logs.
